evidence.note: Blue marks only the current timeline step marker, the agent-run dots (declared by the 'Agent Run' legend), the active nav item and the kicker text, which renders in a darker blue ink; title and body text stay neutral.
One agent's trace is drawn in stronger blue as the focus; past steps' markers revert to grey while the new step's marker is blue.
Red appears only on the broken/unlocked lock badge after the zero-day: an alarm/compromise state.
Red dot marks the mirror crash and the unlocked lock; on step 6 (1920x1080) the lock returns to blue/neutral once rebuilt, so red tracks state rather than decoration.

Card diagrams reuse blue for the agent circle, its path, the captured flag and the scorer pill; the red x marks the blocked attempt. The scorer pill fill is the closest to decorative accent use but highlights the mechanism being explained.
Insight card is neutral text on white; no role colour used for emphasis.

rationale: Blue consistently carries focus/agent identity (current step, active trace, legend-declared agent runs) and red appears only for alarm states (compromised lock, crash, blocked attempt), reverting when the state clears. No heading or body text uses the alarm colour and no colour clashes; the scorer pill is a marginal accent use within the focused mechanism, not a role swap.
